text: A small liquid drop of radius $R$ is divided into 27 identical liquid drops. If the surface tension is $T$, then the work done in the process will be:

solution.body:
Volume constant

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{4}{3}πR^{3}=27\times \dfrac{4}{3}\times πr^{3} \\ R^{3}=27r^{3} \\ R=3r \\ r=\dfrac{R}{3} \\ r^{2}=\dfrac{R^{2}}{9} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \text{Work done}=T.\Delta A \\ =27T\left (4πr^{2}\right )-T4πR^{2} \\ =27T4π\dfrac{R^{2}}{9}-4πR^{2}T \\ =8πR^{2}T \end{array}$

text:
A bob of mass '$m$' is suspended by a light string of length '$L$'. It is imparted a minimum horizontal velocity at the lowest point $A$ such that it just completes half circle reaching the top most position B. The ratio of kinetic energies $\frac{(K.E)_{A}}{(K.E)_{B}}$ is :

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Apply energy conservation between A & B

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{mV}_{\mathrm{L}}^{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{mV}_{\mathrm{H}}^{2}+\mathrm{mg}(2\mathrm{L}) \\ \because \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{L}}=\sqrt{5\mathrm{gL}} \end{array}$

So, $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{H}}=\sqrt{\mathrm{gL}}$

$\frac{(\mathrm{K}.\mathrm{E})_{\mathrm{A}}}{(\mathrm{K}.\mathrm{E})_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{m}(\sqrt{5\mathrm{gL}})^{2}}{\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{m}(\sqrt{\mathrm{gL}})^{2}}=\frac{5}{1}$

text: If the distance between object and its two times magnified virtual image produced by a curved mirror is $15\mathrm{cm}$, the focal length of the mirror must be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A mirror forms a virtual image behind itself, on the side opposite the object. With the object at distance $x$ in front of the mirror, $u=-x$. A virtual, erect image has magnification $+2$:

$m=-\dfrac{v}{u}=2\Rightarrow v=-2u=+2x$

So the image lies $2x$ behind the mirror. The object and the image are on opposite sides of the mirror, so

$x+2x=15\Rightarrow x=5\text{cm},u=-5\text{cm},v=+10\text{cm}$

Mirror formula:

$\dfrac{1}{f}=\dfrac{1}{v}+\dfrac{1}{u}=\dfrac{1}{10}-\dfrac{1}{5}=-\dfrac{1}{10}\Rightarrow f=-10\text{cm}$

The negative focal length means a concave mirror, the only mirror that gives a magnified virtual image.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: A particle is moving in a straight line. The variation of position '$x$' as a function of time '$t$' is given as $x=\left (t^{3}-6t^{2}+20t+15\right )m$. The velocity of the body when its acceleration becomes zero is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The position equation is given by:

$x=t^{3}-6t^{2}+20t+15$

First, compute the velocity $v$ by differentiating the position function with respect to time:

$\frac{dx}{dt}=v=3t^{2}-12t+20$

Next, compute the acceleration $a$ by differentiating the velocity function with respect to time:

$\frac{dv}{dt}=a=6t-12$

We need to find the time $t$ when the acceleration is zero:

$6t-12=0$

$t=2\sec$

Now, find the velocity at $t=2\sec$:

$v=3(2)^{2}-12(2)+20$

$v=8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : Most of the mass of the atom and all its positive charge are concentrated in a tiny nucleus and the electrons revolve around it, is Rutherford's model.

Statement II : An atom is a spherical cloud of positive charges with electrons embedded in it, is a special case of Rutherford's model.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

solution.body:

According to Thomson atomic model, atom is spherical cloud of positive charge with electron embedded in it.

Hence, Statement I is true but statement II false.

text: Two particles $X$ and $Y$ having equal charges are being accelerated through the same potential difference. Thereafter they enter normally in a region of uniform magnetic field and describe circular paths of radii $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ respectively. The mass ratio of $X$ and $Y$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A particle of charge $q$ accelerated through a potential difference $V$ gains kinetic energy $qV$, so its momentum is $p=\sqrt{2mqV}$.

In the magnetic field it moves on a circle of radius

$R=\dfrac{mv}{qB}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2mqV}}{qB}$

With $q$, $V$ and $B$ the same for both particles, $R\propto \sqrt{m}$, so $m\propto R^{2}$:

$\dfrac{m_{X}}{m_{Y}}=\left (\dfrac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}\right )^{2}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: In a single slit diffraction pattern, a light of wavelength 6000$A^{o}$ is used. The distance between the first and third minima in the diffraction pattern is found to be $3\mathrm{mm}$ when the screen in placed $50\mathrm{cm}$ away from slits. The width of the slit is $_________$ $\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $\mathrm{n}^{\text{th}}$ minima

$\mathrm{b}\sin θ=\mathrm{n}λ$

($λ$ is small so $\sin θ$ is small, hence $\sin θ\simeq \tan θ$)

$\mathrm{btan}θ=\mathrm{n}λ$

$\mathrm{b}\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{D}}=\mathrm{n}λ$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{y}_{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}λ\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{b}}\left (\text{Position of}\mathrm{n}^{\mathrm{th}}\text{minima)} \right.$


[IMG]


$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{B}\to 1^{\text{st}}\text{minima,}\mathrm{A}\to 3^{\mathrm{rd}}\text{minima} \\ \mathrm{y}_{3}=\dfrac{3λ\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{b}},\mathrm{y}_{1}=\dfrac{λ\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{b}} \\ \Delta \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{y}_{3}-\mathrm{y}_{1}=\dfrac{2λ\mathrm{D}}{\mathrm{b}} \\ 3\times 10^{-3}=\dfrac{2\times 6000\times 10^{-10}\times 0.5}{\mathrm{b}} \\ \mathrm{b}=\dfrac{2\times 6000\times 10^{-10}\times 0.5}{3\times 10^{-3}} \\ \mathrm{b}=2\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{m} \\ x=2 \end{array}$

text: Hydrogen atom is bombarded with electrons accelerated through a potential difference of $\mathrm{V}$, which causes excitation of hydrogen atoms. If the experiment is being performed at $\mathrm{T}=0\mathrm{K}$, the minimum potential difference needed to observe any Balmer series lines in the emission spectra will be $\frac{α}{10}\mathrm{V}$, where $α=$ $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For minimum potential difference electron has to make transition from $n=3$ to $n=2$ state but first electron has to reach to $\mathrm{n}=3$ state from ground state. So, energy of bombarding electron should be equal to energy difference of $\mathrm{n}=3$ and $\mathrm{n}=1$ state.

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{E}=13.6\left [1-\dfrac{1}{3^{2}}\right ]\mathrm{e}=\mathrm{eV} \\ \dfrac{13.6\times 8}{9}=\mathrm{V} \\ \mathrm{V}=12.09\mathrm{V}\approx 12.1\mathrm{V} \end{array}$

So, $α=121$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift

text: A simple harmonic oscillator has an amplitude $A$ and time period $6π$ second. Assuming the oscillation starts from its mean position, the time required by it to travel from $x=$ A to $x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ A will be $\frac{π}{x}\mathrm{s}$, where $x=$ $_________$.

solution.body:

From phasor diagram particle has to move from $\mathrm{P}$ to $\mathrm{Q}$ in a circle of radius equal to amplitude of SHM.

$\begin{array}{l} \cos 𝜙=\dfrac{\frac{\sqrt{3}\mathrm{A}}{2}}{\mathrm{A}}=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ 𝜙=\dfrac{π}{6} \end{array}$

text:
Two metallic wires $P$ and $Q$ have same volume and are made up of same material. If their area of cross sections are in the ratio $4:1$ and force $F_{1}$ is applied to $P$, an extension of $\Delta l$ is produced. The force which is required to produce same extension in $Q$ is $\mathrm{F}_{2}$.

 The value of $\frac{F_{1}}{F_{2}}$ is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Y}=\frac{\text{Stress}}{\text{Strain}}=\frac{\mathrm{F}/\mathrm{A}}{\Delta \ell /\ell }=\frac{\mathrm{F}\ell }{\mathrm{A}\Delta \ell }$

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \ell =\dfrac{\mathrm{F}\ell }{\mathrm{AY}} \\ \mathrm{V}=\mathrm{A}\ell \Rightarrow \ell =\dfrac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{A}} \\ \Delta \ell =\dfrac{\mathrm{FV}}{\mathrm{A}^{2}\mathrm{Y}} \end{array}$

$Y&V$ is same for both the wires

$\begin{array}{l} \Delta \ell \propto \dfrac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{A}^{2}} \\ \dfrac{\Delta \ell _{1}}{\Delta \ell _{2}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{F}_{1}}{\mathrm{A}_{1}^{2}}\times \dfrac{\mathrm{A}_{2}^{2}}{\mathrm{F}_{2}} \\ \Delta \ell _{1}=\Delta \ell _{2} \\ \mathrm{F}_{1}\mathrm{A}_{2}^{2}=\mathrm{F}_{2}\mathrm{A}_{1}^{2} \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{F}_{1}}{\mathrm{F}_{2}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{A}_{1}^{2}}{\mathrm{A}_{2}^{2}}=\left (\dfrac{4}{1}\right )^{2}=16 \end{array}$

text: A particle is moving in a circle of radius $50\mathrm{cm}$ in such a way that at any instant the normal and tangential components of it's acceleration are equal. If its speed at $\mathrm{t}=0$ is $4\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$, the time taken to complete the first revolution will be $\frac{1}{α}\left [1-e^{-2π}\right ]\mathrm{s}$, where $α=$ $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Equal normal and tangential accelerations, with the speed increasing (as the given form of the time requires), give

$\dfrac{dv}{dt}=\dfrac{v^{2}}{r},r=0.5\text{m}$

Separating variables from $v=4\text{m s}^{-1}$ at $t=0$:

$\int\limits _{4}^{v}\dfrac{dv}{v^{2}}=\int\limits _{0}^{t}\dfrac{dt}{0.5}\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{v}=2t\Rightarrow v=\dfrac{4}{1-8t}$

Distance covered in time $t$:

$s=\int\limits _{0}^{t}\dfrac{4~dt}{1-8t}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln (1-8t)$

One revolution is $s=2πr=π\text{m}$:

$-\dfrac{1}{2}\ln (1-8t)=π\Rightarrow 1-8t=e^{-2π}\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{1}{8}\left [1-e^{-2π}\right ]\text{s}$

Comparing with $\dfrac{1}{α}\left [1-e^{-2π}\right ]$ gives $α=8$.

Hence, the answer is 8.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 29th January Evening Shift
